products.name: Roborock Q7 L5

specs_extra.Dock: Charging dock only (empty the bin by hand)
specs_extra.Smart features: No-go zones, room scheduling, child lock

products.spec_sources: Amazon listing + us.roborock.com (height 3.89 in, 3,200 mAh). The Amazon listing also carries older reviews of the Roborock E4.

editorial.tagline: LiDAR mapping and 8,000 Pa for about $140.
editorial.summary: The cheapest way into a robot that actually maps your home: LiDAR navigation, 8,000 Pa, anti-tangle brushes, a light mop and 150 minutes of runtime — without a self-emptying dock.
body: The Q7 L5 brings Roborock's LiDAR navigation to a budget price. It maps multiple floors, cleans room by room and lets you draw no-go zones in the app, which is what separates it from the random-bounce robots at this price.

Suction is 8,000 Pa with anti-tangle main and side brushes, and a 270 ml tank lets it mop lightly at the same time. The pad doesn't lift, so it can't mop and vacuum rugs in one run, and there's no obstacle camera — pick up cables and socks first.

There's no self-emptying dock, so you'll empty the bin by hand every few runs. At 3.89 in tall it fits under most sofas. With 16,000+ ratings it's one of the most-reviewed robots on Amazon, though the listing mixes in reviews of older Roborock models.
pros: LiDAR mapping at a budget price
editorial.ideal_for: Apartments and small homes that want real mapping on a tight budget.
editorial.not_for: Homes with lots of floor clutter, rugs you don't want wet, or anyone who hates emptying bins.
editorial.verdict: The best cheap robot vacuum with real mapping — just empty it yourself.
editorial.review_summary: 4.0★ from 16,367 ratings (73% 4–5 stars). Owners call it great value and easy to set up, and some say it never gets stuck. Complaints include a unit that kept falling down a step near its dock. The listing includes older reviews of previous Roborock models.

products.name: Tikom L8000 Plus

specs_extra.Carpet: Auto suction boost; remove mop holder or set a no-mop zone before carpets

products.spec_sources: Amazon listing + Vacuum Wars and robot-review.com for height (3.7 in), 18 mm climbing and warranty.

editorial.tagline: A LiDAR robot with a 90-day self-emptying dock for about $210.
editorial.summary: 6,000 Pa, LiDAR mapping, a 3 L self-emptying dock and 150 minutes of runtime — one of the cheapest ways to stop emptying the bin by hand.
body: Tikom's L8000 Plus pairs LiDAR mapping (up to five floors) with a self-emptying dock whose 3 L bag lasts up to 90 days. That combination usually costs more, which is why owners call it the best robot for the price.

Suction is 6,000 Pa with an automatic boost on carpet. It can mop with a basic pad, but the pad doesn't lift, so you need to remove it or set no-mop zones before it reaches rugs. There's no obstacle camera, and it climbs thresholds up to about 0.7 in.
Owners with heavy shedders — including a 100 lb German Shepherd — are happy with how much hair it picks up. It's quiet, works with Alexa and supports 5 GHz Wi-Fi, which many robots don't.
pros: Self-emptying dock (90 days) at a budget price
editorial.ideal_for: Pet owners on a budget who want hands-free emptying.
editorial.not_for: Homes with high thresholds or cluttered floors.
editorial.verdict: The best-value self-emptying robot here — hard to beat for about $210.
editorial.review_summary: 4.5★ from 649 ratings (88% 4–5 stars). Owners praise the accurate map, quiet operation, room selection and how much pet hair it collects (including homes with four dogs). Few complaints so far.

products.name: Dreame D20 Air Plus

specs_extra.Dust bag: 4 L sealed bag, up to 120 days

products.spec_sources: Amazon listing + ca.dreametech.com (height 94.7 mm, 3,200 mAh, 3-year warranty).

editorial.tagline: 20,000 Pa and a 120-day dock for under $230.
editorial.summary: The most suction per dollar in our catalog: 20,000 Pa, LiDAR, anti-tangle brushes and a 4 L self-emptying bag that lasts up to four months — sold by Amazon with a 3-year warranty.
body: The D20 Air Plus takes numbers you used to see on $600 robots — 20,000 Pa of suction and a 120-day self-emptying dock — and sells them for around $230. LiDAR mapping, anti-tangle brushes and edge-focused paths round it out.

It mops with a simple pad and an electronic water tank at the same time as it vacuums. The pad doesn't lift, so it isn't a real vacuum-and-mop for homes with rugs, and there's no obstacle avoidance beyond bump sensors.

At 3.73 in tall it slips under most furniture. Owners find setup quick (one called it under five minutes), though an older review mentions Wi-Fi trouble at first. Dreame backs it with a 3-year warranty, and Amazon sells it directly.
editorial.ideal_for: Most homes that want strong vacuuming and hands-free emptying on a budget.
editorial.not_for: Anyone who wants proper mopping or a robot that dodges clutter.
editorial.verdict: Our top budget pick: flagship suction and a four-month dock for under $250.
editorial.review_summary: 4.2★ from 3,650 ratings (80% 4–5 stars). Owners praise the strong suction, easy mapping and large dust bag, and say it's quieter than older Dreames. One long-term owner had trouble connecting to Wi-Fi at first but says it works great afterwards.

specs_extra.Brushes: JawScrapers main brush + zero-tangle side brush

editorial.tagline: Roborock's best-selling self-emptying robot, with 25,000+ ratings.
editorial.summary: 10,000 Pa, PreciSense LiDAR, dual anti-tangle brushes and a RockDock that holds 7–9 weeks of debris — a proven, simple self-emptying robot.
body: The Q7 M5+ is the upgrade to Roborock's long-running Q5 Max+. It pairs 10,000 Pa of suction and PreciSense LiDAR mapping with a self-emptying dock whose 2.7 L bag lasts about seven to nine weeks.

Its JawScrapers main brush and zero-tangle side brush are designed for pet hair. It can mop at the same time with a detachable pad and three water levels, but owners say to keep expectations realistic: you wash the pad by hand, and there's no obstacle avoidance.

At 3.9 in tall with 2 cm threshold climbing, it suits most homes. It's one of the most-reviewed robots on Amazon (though the listing includes reviews of older models), and it's sold by a third-party seller shipping from Amazon.
cons: Mop pad is washed by hand
editorial.ideal_for: Pet homes that want dependable vacuuming and hands-free emptying.
editorial.not_for: Anyone who wants real mopping or clutter avoidance.
editorial.verdict: A proven self-emptying workhorse, but the Dreame D20 Air Plus gives more for less.

editorial.tagline: A full self-washing, self-emptying station for about $430.
editorial.summary: 26,000 Pa, dual spinning mops that lift 10.5 mm and reach edges, 212°F hot-water mop washing, hot-air drying and a 100-day dust bag — the cheapest all-in-one dock in our catalog.
body: MOVA (a Dreame sister brand) packs a flagship-style dock into a mid-range price. The station empties the robot into a 3.2 L bag for up to 100 days, washes the mops with 212°F water, dries them with hot air and dispenses detergent automatically.

The robot has 26,000 Pa of suction, a triple anti-tangle system for pet hair and two spinning mops that press down with 12 N, extend toward walls and lift 10.5 mm over rugs. A front line laser handles obstacle detection, which is a step below the camera systems on pricier robots.

At 4.09 in it's one of the taller robots here, so check your sofa clearance. Owners with pets call it the best bang for the buck, while one reviewer warns to read the warranty terms carefully after a failure; MOVA lists a 3-year warranty.
pros: All-in-one dock with 212°F mop washing and hot-air drying
Mops lift 10.5 mm and reach edges
editorial.ideal_for: Mixed-floor homes and pet owners who want a fully hands-free station on a mid budget.
editorial.not_for: Low furniture (under ~4.2 in) or cluttered floors.
editorial.verdict: The cheapest full-feature dock we've seen — outstanding value if it fits under your furniture.
editorial.review_summary: 4.1★ from 335 ratings (78% 4–5 stars). Owners praise the suction on pet hair, the hot-water mop washing and the value compared with pricier robots; one says it lifts its mops over mats. A 1-star reviewer warns buyers to check the warranty after a failure.

editorial.tagline: Flagship cleaning with extendable brush and mop for $500.
editorial.summary: 25,000 Pa, a side brush and mop that extend into corners, structured-light obstacle avoidance, 231 minutes of runtime and a self-emptying, self-washing, hot-air-drying dock — sold by Amazon with a 3-year warranty.
body: The L40 Ultra Gen 2 is Dreame's best-selling all-rounder. Both the side brush and one of the spinning mops swing outward to reach corners and under cabinet edges, which owners single out as its best trick.

25,000 Pa of suction with four carpet modes, 10.5 mm mop lifting and structured-light obstacle avoidance make it comfortable in mixed-floor homes. Its 5,200 mAh battery is rated for up to 231 minutes (about 1,679 ft² in quiet mode).

The dock empties the bin, washes the mops and dries them with hot air; an auto-detergent module is an optional extra. At $500 (from $750) it's one of the best-reviewed all-in-one robots in its price range, with 84% 4–5 star ratings.
pros: Extending side brush and mop for corners
cons: One long-term owner wants more battery
editorial.ideal_for: Most homes with hard floors and some rugs that want one robot to do everything.
editorial.verdict: Our favorite all-rounder: flagship features at a mid-range price.
editorial.review_summary: 4.3★ from 612 ratings (84% 4–5 stars). Owners praise the strong suction, even mopping, corner cleaning and slim dock. A two-year owner wishes the battery lasted longer. Former Roomba users say it's a big step up.

products.name: Roborock Qrevo S Pro

specs_extra.Brushes: Zero-tangle side brush, all-rubber main brush, easy-clean omni wheel

products.spec_sources: Amazon listing + us.roborock.com (height 3.8 in, 5,200 mAh, 1-year warranty). Listing shares reviews with related Roborock models.

editorial.summary: 18,500 Pa, zero-tangle brushes, liftable spinning mops, structured-light obstacle avoidance and a dock that empties, refills, washes mops at 167°F and dries them — with 6,000+ bought a month.
body: The Qrevo S Pro is the robot most shoppers end up with in the $500 range. Its dock empties the dust bin, refills the robot's water, washes the mops with 167°F water and dries them with warm air, so day-to-day maintenance is limited to changing a bag every couple of months.

18,500 Pa of suction with zero-tangle side and main brushes handles pet hair well — one owner with a husky, an Aussie and a cat calls it the best Amazon purchase in years. Reactive Tech structured light avoids shoes and toys, and the mops lift for carpets.

At 3.8 in tall it fits under most beds. The main complaint is software: a 1-star owner of eight months says firmware problems made the robot unreliable. It's sold by a third-party seller, and the listing mixes in reviews of related models.
pros: Full dock: empty, refill, 167°F wash, warm-air dry
editorial.ideal_for: Pet households that want a fully hands-free robot at a mainstream price.
editorial.not_for: Anyone who wants a longer warranty (Dreame and MOVA offer 3 years).
editorial.verdict: A safe, popular all-in-one pick — the L40 Gen 2 edges it on corners and warranty.
editorial.review_summary: 4.1★ from 6,413 ratings (76% 4–5 stars). Owners with multiple pets and multi-level homes are very happy, and long-time robot owners call it their best yet. The main complaint is firmware and app reliability after several months.

editorial.tagline: A roller mop that scrubs with clean water, at $499.
editorial.summary: 30,000 Pa, a 10.6-inch roller mop rinsed with fresh water while it cleans, structured light plus AI camera, 15 mm mop lift and a hot-water, hot-air dock — sold by Amazon.
body: The T90 Pro Omni swaps spinning pads for ECOVACS' OZMO Roller: a 10.6-inch roller that's continuously rinsed with clean water and pressed onto the floor, so it scrubs sticky spills instead of smearing them. TruEdge pushes the roller 0.6 in past the body to reach baseboards.

Suction is 30,000 Pa with ZeroTangle 4.0 brushes, and a structured-light sensor plus AI camera handles obstacles. The roller lifts 15 mm for carpets and it climbs 24 mm thresholds (4 cm when stacked).

The dock empties the bin, washes the roller with hot water, dries it with hot air and refills detergent. Owners praise its fast, accurate mapping. At $499 (from $800) and sold by Amazon, it's one of the strongest mopping robots per dollar.
pros: Self-rinsing roller mop scrubs better than pads

editorial.tagline: Roborock's 2026 all-rounder: auto-detaching mops and FlexiArm edges.
editorial.summary: 20,000 Pa, zero-tangle brushes, FlexiArm edge mopping, mops that lift 15 mm or detach for carpets, a 253-minute battery and a hot-wash, warm-air-dry dock.
body: The Qrevo 2 Pro is the 2026 update to Roborock's Qrevo Pro. Its biggest upgrade for mixed floors is carpet handling: it can drop its mops at the dock, vacuum carpets first and lift the mops up to 15 mm when it has to cross rugs.

The FlexiArm edge mop swings out to within 1.85 mm of walls and cabinet kick plates, and a reversible side brush reaches into corners. 20,000 Pa of suction with the Dual Zero-Tangle system handles long hair, and structured-light obstacle avoidance steers around shoes and toys.

Rated for 253 minutes and 54 dB, it's long-running and quiet. Owners of the Qrevo Pro line praise the edge mopping; one 1-star reviewer had a LiDAR failure after about 18 months. It's sold by a third-party seller.
editorial.ideal_for: Homes with lots of rugs and hard floors that want the best carpet handling in the mid range.
editorial.not_for: Buyers who prefer Amazon as the seller.
editorial.verdict: The smartest carpet handling under $600 — a step up from the Qrevo S Pro.

specs_extra.Brushes: Dual rubber anti-tangle brushes + anti-tangle edge-sweeping brush

products.spec_sources: Amazon listing (dimensions 13.77 × 13.58 × 4.13 in, 120 min) + irobot.com (6,000 mAh LFP, 1-year warranty). Listing includes older Roomba reviews.

editorial.tagline: iRobot's pet-hair specialist: dual rubber brushes, 30,000 Pa, no mop.
editorial.summary: A vacuum-only Roomba built for pet hair: dual rubber anti-tangle brushes, 30,000 Pa, LiDAR plus AI-camera obstacle avoidance and a 90-day AutoEmpty dock with odor-control bags.
body: The Roomba Max 715 is for people who want vacuuming done extremely well and don't need mopping. iRobot's dual rubber brushes flex to stay in contact with carpet and hard floors, and resist hair wrap better than bristle brushes — the reason pet owners have long favored Roombas.

It pairs 30,000 Pa and Carpet Boost with ClearView Pro LiDAR mapping and PrecisionVision AI obstacle avoidance, which spots cords and pet messes. The AutoEmpty dock holds about 90 days of debris in AllergenLock bags that trap odors.

At 4.13 in it's the tallest robot here, so check clearance under your furniture. Owners with carpeted upstairs floors and those burned by cheaper robots getting stuck are the happiest; runtime is 120 minutes.
pros: Dual rubber brushes excel on pet hair
AI camera avoids cords and pet messes
editorial.ideal_for: Carpeted homes and heavy shedders that don't need mopping.
editorial.not_for: Hard-floor homes that want mopping, or low furniture.
editorial.verdict: The best pure vacuum for pet hair — skip it if you want mopping.

specs_extra.FlowWash mop: 16 nozzles, 80 RPM, 12 N; dirty water recycled in real time

products.spec_sources: Amazon listing (height 3.74 in, 210 min, 55.8 dB, 1-year warranty) + us.narwal.com (5,200 mAh, 12 mm lift). New listing: only 35 ratings, posted within a few weeks.

editorial.tagline: A 10.5-inch track mop and 31,000 Pa in a 3.74 in body.
editorial.summary: 31,000 Pa, a wide FlowWash track mop that rinses itself as it cleans, a tangle-free brush for long hair, a 120-day dock with warm-air drying — very new, with only 35 ratings.
body: Narwal's Freo 20 Edge uses a 10.5-inch track mop fed by 16 water nozzles and pressed down with 12 N. A scraper pulls dirty water off the mop in real time, so it keeps scrubbing with clean water — similar in spirit to ECOVACS' roller.

Suction is 31,000 Pa, the highest in its price range, and the DualFlow tangle-free system is rated for hair up to 15.7 in long. The mop extends 1.9 in toward baseboards and lifts 12 mm, and structured light recognizes 150+ object types.

The dock holds 120 days of dust and dries the mop with 113°F air. It's promising, but the listing is new: all 35 ratings were posted within a few weeks, which is too few to judge long-term reliability. It's sold by a third-party seller.
editorial.ideal_for: Early adopters with long-haired pets and lots of hard floors.
editorial.not_for: Buyers who want a long track record.
editorial.verdict: Impressive on paper; wait for more owner reviews or buy knowing it's new.

products.availability: Only 2 left in stock · 1K+ bought last month

specs.mop_type: Sonic pad (lifts over carpet, left at base when vacuuming)

specs_extra.Self-refill: Refills the robot's water for up to 30 days

specs_extra.Suction: Shark doesn't publish a Pa figure

editorial.tagline: The most hands-free dock here: it refills its own water.
editorial.summary: Self-empties for 60 days, refills its own water tank for up to 30 days, washes and dries the pad, and lifts itself over thresholds up to about 1.5 in — but at capture it was sold by a third-party seller at a high price.
body: Shark's NeverTouch Pro base does more than most: it empties the robot, refills its water tank automatically for up to 30 days, and washes and dries the mopping pad after each clean. The robot leaves the pad at the base when it only needs to vacuum.

PowerDetect tech boosts suction on dirty spots, blows air jets to push debris out of edges and extends the pad about an inch while mopping. NeverStuck lets it lift itself over obstacles and thresholds — about 1.5 in in Vacuum Wars' testing, the best climbing in our catalog alongside Dreame's X60.

Shark doesn't publish suction in Pa or the robot's height, so we can't score those. Owners with heavy shedders are very happy, but 15% of ratings are 1-star (mop failures, clogs, getting stuck). At capture it was $1,199.99 from a third-party seller, well above its usual price — check before buying.
pros: Pad left at base for vacuum-only runs
editorial.ideal_for: Homes with high thresholds that want the least possible maintenance.
editorial.not_for: Buyers paying far above the usual price, or low furniture (height unknown).
editorial.verdict: Genuinely hands-free and a great climber — only worth it at a normal price.

products.name: Roborock Saros 10R

specs.voice: Hello Rocky, Alexa, Siri, Google Home

specs_extra.Climbing: 4 cm is Roborock's figure for two stacked thresholds; TechRadar measured about 1 cm on a single step
specs_extra.Cables: VertiBeam lateral avoidance cleans along cords

products.spec_sources: Amazon listing + us.roborock.com/pages/roborock-saros-10r (79.8 mm height, 22 mm mop lift) + TechRadar review. Listing includes older Roborock reviews.

editorial.tagline: 3.14 inches tall: it cleans where turret robots can't.
editorial.summary: No LiDAR turret, so it's just 3.14 in tall — with 22,000 Pa, camera plus 3D obstacle avoidance that cleans along cables, 22 mm mop lift and a full self-cleaning dock.
body: The Saros 10R replaces the usual LiDAR bump on top with Roborock's StarSight 2.0 solid-state sensors, bringing the robot down to 3.14 in. That's the difference between cleaning under a low sofa or bed and stopping at its edge.

VertiBeam side sensing and an RGB camera recognize 108 obstacle types and let it clean right along cables instead of avoiding the whole area. 22,000 Pa with zero-tangle brushes handles hair, and the twin mops lift 22 mm or detach for carpet.

The dock empties, washes and dries. Roborock claims 4 cm climbing over stacked thresholds, but TechRadar measured far less on a single step, so don't count on it for tall thresholds. At $1,100 (from $1,600) from a third-party seller, you pay a premium mainly for the slim body.
pros: Cleans along cables with camera + 3D sensing
editorial.ideal_for: Homes with low sofas and beds that turret robots can't reach.
editorial.not_for: Budget buyers or homes with tall thresholds.
editorial.verdict: The robot to buy if your furniture is low — otherwise the mid-range docks are better value.

specs.obstacle_avoidance: Dual AI cameras + side 3D structured light (280+ objects)

products.spec_sources: Amazon listing (3.13 in, 180 min, 3-year warranty) + dreametech.com + Vacuum Wars review (6,400 mAh, climbing).

editorial.tagline: The thinnest, strongest, best-climbing robot in our catalog.
editorial.summary: 3.13 in tall with a retractable LiDAR, 35,000 Pa, dual AI cameras, 4.5 cm threshold climbing, extending mops and a dock that does everything — at $1,500.
body: The X60 Max Ultra Complete is Dreame's everything robot. A retractable LiDAR drops it to 3.13 in so it slides under low furniture, yet it can still climb single thresholds up to 4.5 cm — and step up to 8.8 cm with stacked thresholds.

35,000 Pa DuoBrush suction, dual AI cameras with side structured light (280+ object types) and a RoboSwing mop that extends into corners make it the most capable cleaner here. The mops press at 15 N with warm water.

Its dock washes mops with 212°F water, dries them with hot air, holds 100 days of dust, refills itself and doses two cleaning solutions. It has a 3-year warranty and Amazon sells it. Owners say it rarely gets stuck; one 1-star reviewer found its navigation chaotic and returned it.
editorial.ideal_for: Large homes with low furniture, thresholds and mixed floors — and a big budget.
editorial.not_for: Anyone whose home a $500 all-in-one already handles.
editorial.verdict: The best robot vacuum money can buy right now, if you need what it does.
editorial.review_summary: 4.2★ from 270 ratings (82% 4–5 stars). Owners say it handles tricky areas and edges without getting stuck and transitions smoothly between floors and carpet. One notes the step climbing only helps for a couple of inches; a 1-star reviewer returned it over erratic navigation.

products.spec_sources: Amazon listing (2.99 in per the bullets; the spec table says 2.8 in). Lefant doesn't publish a suction figure on the listing.

editorial.tagline: A 2.99 in, tangle-free robot vacuum for about $90.
editorial.summary: The cheapest robot in our catalog: a slim 2.99 in body, a brushless suction port that pet hair can't wrap around, app and voice control and 120 minutes of runtime. No mapping and no dock.
body: The Lefant M210 is a basic robot that does one job: keep hard floors free of dust and pet hair between real cleanings. There's no roller brush, just a suction port, so long hair goes straight into the bin instead of wrapping.

It doesn't map your home. It uses a gyroscope and infrared sensors to run zigzag or random patterns, and the app lets you schedule runs and change suction. Owners say it gets confused when furniture moves and struggles with some debris, but it's durable and easy to live with.

At 2.99 in it's one of the slimmest robots here, so it reaches under most beds and sofas. Lefant doesn't publish suction, and the 120-minute runtime is measured on low power, so our suction score is zero until it does.
editorial.ideal_for: Small apartments with hard floors and pets, on the smallest budget.
editorial.not_for: Large homes, thick carpet, or anyone who wants room-by-room cleaning.
editorial.verdict: The best robot under $100 for hard floors and pet hair — keep expectations basic.
editorial.review_summary: 4.1★ from 16,309 ratings (77% 4–5 stars). Owners call it a great value that handles dust and dog hair on hard floors, and praise how simple and durable it is. Complaints: it misses some debris and gets confused when furniture moves.

editorial.tagline: The simplest robot here: a remote, no app, no Wi-Fi.
editorial.summary: A 2.99 in robot you control with a remote: tangle-free suction port, 120 minutes of runtime and scheduling, with no app, no map and no Wi-Fi to set up.
body: The ILIFE V2 is for people who don't want an app. You press a button or use the remote, it cleans in a random pattern, and it returns to charge when the battery runs low. Scheduling is built in.

Like the Lefant, it uses a suction port with no roller brush, so pet hair doesn't wrap around anything. Owners say it picks up a surprising amount of dog hair on hard floors, but it's weak on carpet and tends to favor some areas while missing others.
It's 2.99 in tall and 69 dB — louder than most. ILIFE doesn't publish a suction figure, and many reviews on the listing are for older ILIFE models.
editorial.ideal_for: Older relatives, renters and anyone who wants push-button cleaning on hard floors.
editorial.not_for: Carpeted homes or anyone who wants full coverage every run.
editorial.verdict: A no-fuss hard-floor helper; the Lefant M210 is the better robot for similar money.
editorial.review_summary: 4.2★ from 24,406 ratings (80% 4–5 stars), including many for older ILIFE models. Recent owners say it handles dog hair on hard floors and is easy to empty. A 3-star review says it struggles on carpet and keeps missing the same areas.

editorial.tagline: A LiDAR Roomba for $149, sold by Amazon.
editorial.summary: iRobot's entry model: LiDAR mapping, straight-row cleaning, room selection, 200 minutes of runtime and a huge bin — but a single bristle brush that struggles with long hair.
body: The Roomba 105 Vac is the cheapest way to get a current-generation Roomba with LiDAR. It maps quickly, cleans in neat rows, lets you pick rooms and keep-out zones in the app, and recharges and resumes when needed.

Owners upgrading from older Roombas say it's quieter, has a much bigger bin and handles area rugs well. Vacuum Wars measured solid carpet cleaning (82% of embedded sand) but poor pet-hair pickup, with most long strands wrapping the single bristle brush.
At 4.1 in it's one of the tallest robots here, there's no obstacle avoidance, and it has no dock to empty itself. Many of its 31,000+ ratings come from the older Roomba 692 that shares the listing.
pros: LiDAR mapping and room selection for $149
cons: Bristle brush tangles with long hair
editorial.ideal_for: Homes without long-haired pets that want a mapping Roomba cheaply.
editorial.not_for: Pet owners, low furniture, or cluttered floors.
editorial.verdict: Good mapping for the money; pet owners should pick the Roborock Q7 L5 instead.
editorial.review_summary: 4.2★ from 31,611 ratings (80% 4–5 stars), shared with older Roomba models. Recent owners say it's the quietest Roomba they've had, maps easily and handles area rugs. Complaints: it gets hung up on clutter, and one owner needed a replacement after three months.

editorial.tagline: The slimmest robot in our catalog at 2.85 in — and one of the quietest.
editorial.summary: A 2.85 in, 55 dB robot vacuum with a remote, BoostIQ carpet boost and 100 minutes of runtime. No app, no map, no dock — just quiet, reliable cleaning under low furniture.
body: The 11S MAX has been one of Amazon's best-selling robots for years because it's slim, quiet and simple. At 2.85 in it's the thinnest robot we list, so it cleans under beds and sofas most others can't reach.
It navigates in a random pattern, boosts suction on carpet automatically and climbs thresholds up to 18 mm. There's no app or Wi-Fi: you use the remote or the buttons, including scheduling.

Suction is the weak spot. eufy has long rated it at 2,000 Pa — far below the budget LiDAR robots — and its bristle roller isn't anti-tangle. With 59,000+ ratings it's proven, but some of those reviews are for other eufy models.
editorial.ideal_for: Very low furniture and people who want a quiet robot without an app.
editorial.not_for: Pet-heavy homes or anyone who wants mapping.
editorial.verdict: Buy it for the 2.85 in height and the quiet; otherwise a LiDAR robot is better value.

editorial.tagline: A self-emptying Roomba that vacuums and mops, at $200 during this deal.
editorial.summary: 15,000 Pa, LiDAR, anti-hair-wrap brushes, a light mop and a 90-day AutoEmpty dock — at 57% off its $469.99 list price when we checked.
body: The Roomba 115X Combo is iRobot's 2026 entry-level vacuum-and-mop, bundled with the AutoEmpty dock. ClearView LiDAR maps the home and cleans in neat rows, and the 2.5 L bag holds up to three months of debris.
It vacuums at 15,000 Pa with anti-hair-wrap brushes and mops lightly with a washable pad at the same time. The pad doesn't lift, so you set no-mop zones to keep rugs dry. There's no obstacle camera.

At $199.99 it undercuts most self-emptying robots with LiDAR. Early owners of this model praise the mapping and the dock, but most of the 5,000+ ratings come from older Roombas on the same listing, and iRobot doesn't publish the robot's height.
editorial.ideal_for: Pet homes with mostly hard floors that want hands-free emptying on a budget.
editorial.not_for: Homes with lots of rugs you'd need to mop around.
editorial.verdict: At $200 it's one of the best deals in robot vacuums; at full price, look elsewhere.
